extracted.intended_audience: ACM SIGMOD Reproducibility reviewers (volunteer reviewers for the SIGMOD reproducibility program)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers validating the reproducibility of SIGMOD papers, including how to assess experimental artifacts, interact with authors and chairs, run experiments, and report results. Focuses on practical steps to reproduce results and produce a short reproducibility report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify hardware and software requirements before accepting
rubrics_metrics.description: Before accepting to review a paper take a look at the experiments, specifically at the hardware and software required to ensure you can fulfill the basic requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check experiment descriptions for required platforms, libraries, hardware, or other resources up front so you can determine whether you are able to run and assess the artifacts. Decline or discuss with the chair if you cannot meet the requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish contact with the paper's contact author
rubrics_metrics.description: The chair of the committee will put you in touch with the contact author of the paper you agreed to review. If necessary initiate a discussion with the authors to ensure you are at the same page regarding specific details in the experiments that may not be clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively ask clarifying questions about ambiguous steps, parameters, or expected outputs before attempting to reproduce results. Use the contact author to resolve uncertainties about experiment procedures or data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quickly verify artifact completeness and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: After you receive access to code, datasets, and scripts, quickly verify that the submission is complete and has enough documentation before proceeding further.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that code, datasets, run scripts, and instructions are present and readable. If essential pieces are missing or documentation is insufficient, request the missing materials or clarifications from the authors before investing more time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage use of reprozip for dependency management
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage authors to use repro-zip that makes it easier to handle software dependencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend tools that package environments and dependencies (e.g., reprozip) to simplify reproducibility and reduce environment-specific issues. Suggest authors provide clear instructions for dependency installation or packaged environments when reprozip is not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact authors immediately when issues appear; expect collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: When an issue appears, immediately contact the authors to help resolve it. The authors’ collaboration is both welcome and expected because they know and understand the specifics of their algorithms and code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise problems early (e.g., failing scripts, missing paths, dependency errors) and work with authors to debug. Many issues are simple (automation, path independence, dependencies) and can be fixed quickly with author assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual goal: reproduce results and provide feedback to create shareable artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal is both to go through the process of reproducing the results and to provide enough feedback to the authors so that they can create a sharable instance of their code and experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond verifying claims, produce actionable suggestions to improve artifact documentation, packaging, and robustness so the authors can publish a reproducible, sharable instance of their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate system interference; use dedicated machines when running experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: When running experiments eliminate any interference in your systems, i.e., make sure, unless otherwise stated by the authors, that the machines used are dedicated to the reproducibility experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid background processes, variable load, or other jobs that could affect timing or resource-sensitive experiments. If authors specify otherwise, follow their instructions; otherwise use isolated/dedicated hardware to reduce variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: If results do not support claims, contact authors to resolve setup/hardware issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If the results you gathered during the reproducibility process do not support the claims, contact the authors to address this. This may be due to issues that have to do with the set-up of the experiments or the hardware specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before concluding non-reproducibility, verify configuration, seeds, data versions, and hardware, and discuss discrepancies with authors to determine whether differences are explainable or fixable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a short reproducibility report (1-2 pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a short report (1-2 pages) to document the results and whether you were able to reproduce the results. If you can reproduce only part of the results please indicate that in your document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document what you ran, exact commands, environment/hardware specs, which results reproduced or failed, and any important setup or analysis details. Communicate the draft report to authors to ensure fairness and incorporate their suggestions before finalizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalate irreproducible papers to the chair
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper cannot be reproduced contact the chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When unresolved issues prevent reproduction despite author collaboration and reasonable effort, notify the committee chair with findings and the reproducibility report for further action.
